This is the short-run ETI that still contains the shifting component; the shifting-free counterpart is claim S4.

claims.notes: The abstract only announces tax salience as an important factor; the direction comes from the introduction and from Section IIC, so support is assembled. Salience is measured by survey-reported awareness (answering both 'after January 1' and 'legal'), hence treatment_relation proxy. The only quantification is the 5.5 percentage point difference between the informed treatment group and the control group, reported in prose for Figure A2 in the online appendix, which is NOT bound into this PDF; no table in this PDF prints an estimate of the effect of awareness on shifting. Table 4 prints only the distribution of survey answers (17 percent of the treatment group informed), which is descriptive and is therefore not extracted as a result. The authors themselves state in the conclusion that 'our analysis cannot establish a causal relationship'.
